question:
Where can you find the type of cells shown in the following figure ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/095e221094a05dec5ce02668c7c289f79f8ec00ae84ab4de214e79fd1efa1335.png]
solution:
The correct answer is** Leaves and Shoots.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shoot**

 
 
• The portion of a plant that** grows above ground **and contains blooming buds, lateral buds, and flowering stems is **called a shoot**.
 
• Functions. It is in charge of a plant's ability to **produce food **or engage in photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Leave**
 
 
• A leaf is a major stem appendage of a vascular plant that is designed specifically for** photosynthesis** and is often carried laterally aboveground.
 
• Leaves are collectively referred to as **"flora,"** as in "fall foliage," whereas the shoot system consists of the leaves, stem, flower, and fruit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Roots**

 
 
• All vascular plants have** substantial subterranean **components called roots.
 
• This area of the plant is primarily in charge of securing it to the **ground **and using the soil's vital nutrients, minerals, and water.
 
• Food is kept in it as well.
 
 
 
• **Flowers**
 
 
• A flower is a flowering plant's **reproductive organ**, sometimes referred to as a bloom or blooming (plants of the division Angiospermae).
 
• In terms of biology, a flower's role in reproduction is to facilitate the union of** sperm and eggs.**
